# PathQ-Former: Final Experimental Report

**Date:** 2026-10-05 | **Status:** campaign complete (204 GPU cohort-level runs + 13 laptop runs, all archived in `pod_results/*.tgz`; every table regenerated by `scripts/reproduce_tables.sh` into `results/final/`); manuscript revised into an audit paper (`paper/tmlr_v2/`); the SurvPath-recipe experiment (Section 14) is implemented but has not been run | **Code:** this repository, v0.3.0 | **Raw record:** `EXPERIMENT_LOG.md`

---

## 0. Executive summary

PathQ-Former is a Q-Former-style fusion model that reads a patient's whole-slide-image (WSI) patch embeddings and RNA-seq pathway tokens through two banks of 32 learned queries, fuses the 64 codes with a small Transformer, and predicts discrete-time survival hazards. A missing modality (at training or test time) is replaced by learned null codes, so one checkpoint serves WSI+RNA, WSI-only and RNA-only patients.

Under a single protocol (SurvPath's 5-fold patient-level splits, disease-specific survival, fixed 20-epoch budget, final checkpoint, 3 seeds, identical for every method) on five TCGA cohorts, every trained checkpoint was re-evaluated with one input removed, with one input permuted across the validation patients, and with a random fraction of patients lacking a modality (the **input-use audit**, Section 5). The unit of analysis for every test is the (cohort, fold) after averaging the seeds (25 pooled units; Section 4.4); the 75 (fold, seed) pairs quoted in earlier versions of this report are not independent, because the seeds of one fold share its validation patients. All numbers are from `results/final/`.

1. **The official SurvPath implementation does not respond to its RNA input.** Permuting the RNA across patients changes its C-index by +0.001 (t p 0.36, Wilcoxon p 0.13); replacing it by the training mean, +0.001. Permuting the slide costs 0.068 (p 0.016 / 0.007) and removing it 0.073 (p 0.003 / 0.002), leaving 0.47-0.52 on every cohort. A high fused C-index does not show that both modalities are used.
2. **Null codes and modality dropout remove the collapse; the auxiliary heads make the fused output respond to RNA.** PathQ-Former without aux heads is as blind to RNA removal as SurvPath (+0.000) but loses only 0.030 without the slide (0.069 when the same checkpoints receive the mean patch embedding instead of the null code, one seed). With aux heads the fused prediction responds to RNA (-0.023 when permuted, p 0.075 / 0.063; -0.013 when removed) against -0.067 when the slide is permuted; the fused risk remains histology-led (Spearman 0.83 with the checkpoint's own RNA-removed risk, 0.45 with its slide-removed risk).
3. **One checkpoint covers incomplete patients.** PathQ-Former keeps 0.54-0.62 with either input removed (RNA removed 0.576-0.600; slide removed 0.538-0.617, three-seed means) and moves by at most 0.025 when half of the patients lack a modality (BRCA 0.622 -> 0.597).
4. **Accuracy at equal budget is parity, not superiority.** Pooled over 25 seed-averaged folds PathQ-Former exceeds SurvPath by +0.036 (95 % CI [-0.004, +0.071]; t p 0.074, Wilcoxon p 0.030; 18/25 folds) and the variant without aux heads by +0.037 ([+0.009, +0.065]; p 0.020 / 0.020; 17/25). Per cohort only BRCA has a raw p < 0.05 (+0.086, t p 0.017) and it does not survive Holm correction (0.084); no DSS cohort does. Against the RNA-only MLP the margins are +0.012 and +0.014 (p >= 0.34) and against the late-fusion ensemble +0.011 and +0.009 (p >= 0.28); the MLP scores higher than PathQ-Former on BRCA and COADREAD. No unimodal baseline differs from SurvPath pooled (ABMIL +0.001, SNN -0.007, MLP +0.024).
5. **Validation-loss early stopping would have hurt the late learners.** Replayed on the 590 stored 20-epoch fold histories (Section 3.3), it selects epoch 1 on median (93 % of folds epoch 1-3) and costs PathQ-Former 0.059, its variant without aux heads 0.090, the slide-only and RNA-only PathQ-Formers 0.065 and 0.034, SNN 0.038 and the MLP 0.027, and SurvPath (+0.000) and ABMIL (-0.001) nothing.
6. **Overall survival (one seed)**: +0.034 over SurvPath ([+0.014, +0.054]; p 0.003 / 0.003); BLCA, the development cohort, is the only cohort that survives Holm, under the t-test only (0.039; Wilcoxon 0.312).
7. **Efficiency:** 16.9 M vs 21.2 M parameters, equal forward latency (35 vs 36 ms/patient), 104 vs 176 ms training step, 1.17 vs 1.74 GiB peak GPU memory on full slides.
8. **Ablations of the final configuration** (BLCA, seed 0, Section 8): 2 bins 0.628, 4 bins 0.625 (0.630 over three seeds), 8 bins 0.609; Reactome+Hallmark 0.625 (seed 0), Xena 0.628, Hallmark-only 0.600; 4096 training patches 0.626 vs all patches 0.625.

Scope of claims: SurvPath was run with its published hyper-parameters and not re-tuned; PathQ-Former's hyper-parameters were developed on BLCA under a 10-epoch budget and the aux-head variant was adopted after the 20-epoch results on all cohorts had been seen, so both variants are co-primary and no accuracy superiority over SurvPath is claimed. The recipe has not been applied to SurvPath (implemented, not run; Section 14).

Total compute: 204 GPU cohort-level runs (about 210 GPU-hours, about 130 USD on Runpod: RTX PRO 4000/4500 and RTX 2000 Ada pods plus a 250 GB network volume) and 13 laptop-CPU runs (roughly 60 hours).

## 1. Method

### 1.1 Architecture (`src/models/pathqformer.py`)

```
WSI patches (frozen UNI2-h, N x 1536)          RNA-seq (4,999 genes) -> 275 pathway tokens
            |                                                   |
   Histology query block (K = 32)                    Genomic query block (K = 32)
   LayerNorm(input) -> [cross-attn -> self-attn -> FFN] x 2 (pre-norm), d = 256, 8 heads
            |  Z_h (32 x 256)                                   |  Z_g (32 x 256)
            +----------------------- [Z_h ; Z_g] ---------------+
                                        |
                       Cross-modal fusion Transformer (2 layers, d = 256)
                                        |
                        attention pooling -> 4 discrete hazards -> NLL-survival loss
```

- **Pathway tokens.** Each of the 275 Reactome + Hallmark pathways (SurvPath's `combine` set; pathways with 3-300 genes) gets its own small MLP (hidden 128) over its member genes; the outputs are the genomic tokens. Alternative sets tested: Xena (281) and Hallmark-only (50).
- **Missing modalities.** A `NullTokenModule` holds a learned 32 x 256 code per modality. An absent modality is replaced by its null code before fusion. During training each present modality is dropped per sample with p = 0.15, never both (`modality_dropout`).
- **Auxiliary unimodal heads** (`aux_heads`, weight 0.5). Two extra survival heads on the pre-fusion codes Z_h and Z_g, each trained with the same NLL on the samples where its modality is present. They force each branch to be prognostic on its own. This is the recommended final configuration (`configs/protocol_fixed/pathq_fast_e20_aux.yaml`).
- **Loss / risk.** Discrete-time NLL-survival loss (Zadeh & Schmid, as in MCAT/SurvPath) over 4 hazard bins, `alpha = 0` for PathQ-Former (0.5 for SurvPath, its published setting). Risk score = -sum_t S(t).
- **Size.** 16.9 M trainable parameters including the pathway tokenizer (SurvPath: 21.2 M).

### 1.2 Training (final configuration)

| Setting | PathQ-Former (+aux) | SurvPath (official code, `data/survpath_repo`) |
|---|---|---|
| Epochs / selection | 20, final checkpoint | 20, final checkpoint |
| Optimizer | RAdam, lr 1e-4, wd 1e-4, 1 warm-up epoch, cosine | RAdam, lr 5e-4 (published), wd 1e-4 |
| Batch | 1 patient, gradient accumulation 2, clip 1.0 | 1 patient |
| Dropout | 0.25 (+ modality dropout 0.15) | 0.1 |
| Patches | all patches of all slides of the patient | 4096-patch subsample (published) |
| Sampling | weighted by (bin, censorship) | same |
| Genes | MinMax to [-1, 1] fit on the training split | same |

Baselines under the identical protocol and budget: **ABMIL** (attention MIL on WSI only), **SNN** (self-normalizing net on the 4,999 genes), **MLP** (two-layer MLP on the genes), all with the SurvPath repository's hyper-parameters, plus **late fusion** (z-scored risk average of a WSI-only and an RNA-only PathQ-Former).

### 1.3 Evaluation protocol (v2)

| Aspect | Choice |
|---|---|
| Unit | patient (`case_id`); all slides of a patient concatenated |
| Splits | SurvPath's exact 5-fold CV splits |
| Endpoint | disease-specific survival (DSS); overall survival (OS) as a secondary experiment |
| Time bins | quartiles of **uncensored training** patients, outer edges +-inf, re-used for validation |
| Primary metric | Harrell's C-index on continuous time (`sksurv.concordance_index_censored`) |
| Also stored per fold | Uno's IPCW C-index truncated at the 75th percentile of training event times; Brier / IBS and time-dependent AUC on the interior quartile grid; 1000x bootstrap 95 % CI; KM log-rank at the median risk split |
| Seeds | `seed + fold`; 3 seeds (0, 1, 2) per cell |
| Statistics | one value per (cohort, fold) = mean over the seeds available for both methods; paired t and exact Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 25 pooled folds with a 95 % percentile-bootstrap CI of the mean difference (10,000 resamples of folds) as the primary test; per-cohort tests (5 folds) Holm-adjusted over the five cohorts and exploratory. Tests over (fold, seed) pairs (15 / 75) are still printed by `scripts/seed_table.py` but are not independent units |
| Audit | same checkpoint tested with RNA or WSI removed (null code for PathQ-Former, training mean for SurvPath and, for comparison, PathQ-Former), with RNA or WSI permuted across the validation patients, with 10 / 20 / 30 / 50 % of patients randomly missing one modality (5 repeats), and its fused risk correlated (Spearman) with its own single-input risks and the other models' risks |

"Mean +- std" in the tables below is the spread over the 3 seeds of the 5-fold mean unless stated otherwise.

## 2. Data

Five TCGA cohorts with UNI2-h patch features (HF `MahmoodLab/UNI2-h-features`, 1536-d, frozen) and SurvPath's RNA/metadata. Patient and event counts as realised by the DSS splits:

| Cohort | Patients | DSS events | Events per validation fold | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLCA (bladder) | 359 | 113 | 16-25 | the only cohort with comfortable event counts |
| BRCA (breast) | 868 | 60 | 7-20 | 93 % censored; largest slides (median ~10k patches) |
| COADREAD (colorectal) | 296 | 37 | 5-13 | fewest events; fold-level C-index very noisy (sd over folds 0.12-0.25 across methods and seeds) |
| HNSC (head and neck) | 392 | 117 | 13-45 | |
| STAD (stomach) | 318 | 84 | 9-33 | |

Low event counts are the dominant source of variance: with 5-9 validation events a single patient reorders the fold's C-index by several points. This is why every table pools over folds and seeds and reports paired tests rather than per-cohort means alone.

## 3. Protocol audit (2026-09-10) and protocol decisions

### 3.1 Six defects in the May pipeline (all fixed; old numbers discarded)

| # | Defect | Effect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | C-index computed on the 4 discrete bins | ~75 % of pairs tied and dropped; not the literature's metric | Harrell's C on continuous months |
| 2 | Bin edges fit separately on train and validation | validation labels on a different scale; leaks the validation label distribution | bins from uncensored training patients, re-used |
| 3 | Slide-level samples (423) | multi-slide patients counted up to 9x; SurvPath is patient-level (359) | one sample per patient |
| 4 | Genes fed unscaled (log values -10..15) | arbitrary input scale for the pathway MLPs | MinMax on train |
| 5 | Selection and reporting on validation C-index; no seeds | optimistic bias; irreproducible fold collapse | selection on val loss or fixed budget; seeded |
| 6 | Risk = 1 - S_last; modality dropout per batch | non-standard risk; wrong batch semantics | risk = -sum S_t; per-sample dropout |

Two evaluation artefacts were also removed: SurvPath's Brier/AUC grid includes the validation min/max time, where one patient at risk gave AUC 0.13 and dragged the mean to 0.37; and the untruncated IPCW C-index explodes when the censoring survival G(t) reaches 0.03 at 120 months. The grid is now the interior quartile edges and Uno's C is truncated at the 75th percentile of training event times.

### 3.2 Why the fixed 20-epoch budget

The first multi-cohort campaign used early stopping on validation loss. On STAD, HNSC and BRCA most methods, including the official SurvPath on HNSC and the RNA baselines, landed near chance (0.45-0.55; 14 of 25 method x cohort cells, Section 3.3), far below the published 0.60-0.75. The histories showed the cause: with 7-45 events per validation fold (BRCA 7-20, STAD 9-33, HNSC 13-45; Table C of `table_selection_rules.txt`) the NLL is noise and val-loss selection picked epoch 1-3 checkpoints for every method while the validation C-index was still rising. This is a protocol failure, not an architecture result.

The fixed budget (train N epochs, report the final checkpoint, the MCAT/SurvPath convention) was adopted because under it the official SurvPath reproduces its published range and is seed-stable (10-epoch budget, `survpath_e10` seeds 0-2: BLCA 0.588 / 0.585 / 0.593; STAD 0.609 / 0.593 / 0.617; `summary_v2_all_runs.md`, `summary_ablate_all_runs.md`). The budget was set to 20 rather than 10 epochs because the pooled per-epoch curves showed PathQ-Former still rising at epoch 10 while SurvPath was flat from epoch 8; at 20 epochs PathQ-Former is ahead at every epoch >= 11 (0.605 vs 0.573 at epoch 20, peaks 0.612 at 13 vs 0.585 at 14, pooled over 35 / 30 fold histories). The budget is identical for all six methods. Best-epoch numbers are always logged as an optimistic bound but never reported as results.

Under the 10-epoch budget PathQ-Former (without aux heads) was already +0.028 over SurvPath pooled over the 25 seed-averaged folds (95 % CI [-0.001, +0.057]; t p 0.079, Wilcoxon p 0.063; 18/25 folds; `table_dss_10ep.txt`, `table_primary_tests.txt`), ahead on BRCA and COADREAD (+0.064, +0.094; COADREAD raw t p 0.015, Holm 0.075) and behind on HNSC and STAD within noise, so the picture does not hinge on the budget choice. The learning rate and gradient-accumulation setting were changed together with the budget, so the 10- and 20-epoch results are not a pure budget comparison.

### 3.3 Post-hoc replay of checkpoint-selection rules (`scripts/posthoc_selection.py` -> `results/final/table_selection_rules.txt`)

Every run stores its per-epoch validation history, so a selection rule can be replayed without training. Table A replays four rules on the stored histories: (i) the final epoch (what the report uses), (ii) validation-loss early stopping with patience 5, (iii) argmin validation loss, (iv) the oracle (best validation C-index, an unattainable bound). Every rule selects on the fold it is scored on, so (ii)-(iv) are biased in favour of selection and the deficit of (ii) is a conservative estimate.

| 20-epoch method (3 seeds; single-modality PathQ-Formers 70 fold histories) | (i) final | (ii) early-stopped | delta (ii)-(i), 25 seed-averaged folds (t p / W p) | epoch selected by (ii) | epoch of best val. C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PathQ-Former + aux heads | 0.604 | 0.546 | -0.059 (0.016 / 8e-4) | 2.2 | 10.0 |
| PathQ-Former | 0.605 | 0.516 | -0.090 (3e-7 / 1e-6) | 1.8 | 9.9 |
| WSI-only PathQ-Former | 0.588 | 0.523 | -0.065 (0.006 / 0.005) | 1.8 | 9.3 |
| RNA-only PathQ-Former | 0.567 | 0.532 | -0.034 (0.062 / 0.080) | 1.4 | 9.7 |
| SurvPath | 0.568 | 0.568 | +0.000 (0.99 / 0.98) | 1.6 | 6.9 |
| ABMIL | 0.569 | 0.568 | -0.001 (0.95 / 0.61) | 1.4 | 6.2 |
| SNN | 0.561 | 0.523 | -0.038 (0.054 / 0.052) | 1.4 | 7.3 |
| RNA MLP | 0.592 | 0.565 | -0.027 (0.078 / 0.075) | 1.2 | 7.2 |

Over the 590 stored fold histories the rule selects epoch 1 on median (mean 1.6; 93 % of folds epoch 1-3) and would have stopped after 6.6 of 20 epochs (patience reached in every fold). The methods that train with a warm-up epoch and the lower learning rate (the PathQ-Formers) reach their best validation C-index at epoch 9.3-10.0 and lose most; SurvPath and ABMIL peak at epoch 6.2-6.9 and lose nothing. Under rule (ii) 23 of the 40 method x cohort cells have a mean C-index within 0.45-0.55, against 5 under the final checkpoint (HNSC 8/8, STAD 7/8, BRCA 4/8). The 10-epoch runs behave the same way (25 seed-averaged folds: PathQ-Former -0.075, t p 8.0e-6 / W p 2.7e-5; SurvPath -0.010, p 0.55 / 0.47; Table B). Table D replays the actual validation-loss campaign of `outputs_v2` (patience 5, min_epochs 6; 29 cohort runs, 145 folds, now including the archived BLCA laptop runs, so seed 0 of every method is present on BLCA and SurvPath and the hybrid have seeds 0-2 there): median selected epoch 1 (82 % of folds epoch 1-3), 7.2 epochs trained, 14 of 25 method x cohort cells within 0.45-0.55 (mean reported C-index 0.543 against an oracle of 0.644); the exceptions on the three cohorts named above are SurvPath on STAD (0.610) and SNN on BRCA (0.572). Table C lists the patients and events per validation fold (5-45 events, median 16).

Per-cohort seed-averaged paired tests vs SurvPath (5 folds each; raw t p and Holm-adjusted p over the five cohorts):

| Cohort | PathQ-Former delta (t p, Holm) | PathQ-Former + aux delta (t p, Holm) |
|---|---|---|
| BLCA | +0.015 (0.52, 1.00) | +0.036 (0.18, 0.70) |

Reading: both PathQ-Former variants are ahead of SurvPath on four cohorts and tied on STAD; the pooled margin of the variant without aux heads is significant under both tests and that of the aux variant under the Wilcoxon test only, and no per-cohort difference survives Holm correction. The tests over the 75 (fold, seed) pairs that earlier versions of this report quoted (t p 0.002 and 0.007) overstate the evidence because the seeds of a fold share its validation patients; `table1_dss_20ep_vs_survpath.txt` prints both. SurvPath's published numbers are for OS with its own preprocessing, so the reference point here is the same code run under our protocol with its published hyper-parameters, which were not re-tuned.

### 4.2 Table 2: the same runs with the RNA MLP as reference

| Method | BLCA | BRCA | COADREAD | HNSC | STAD | Pooled, 25 seed-averaged folds: delta [95 % CI], t p / W p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PathQ-Former | -0.002 | -0.016 | +0.004 | +0.020 | +0.062 (p 0.32) | +0.014 [-0.023, +0.049], 0.47 / 0.37 |
| PathQ-Former + aux | +0.019 | -0.005 | -0.020 | +0.028 | +0.041 | +0.012 [-0.022, +0.044], 0.47 / 0.34 |
| SurvPath | -0.017 | -0.091 | -0.064 | -0.003 | +0.056 | -0.024 [-0.077, +0.027], 0.38 / 0.41 |

A two-layer MLP on the 4,999 genes, run with repository defaults, is a baseline that the multimodal literature rarely reports at equal budget. Neither fusion variant is detectably better than it pooled, and the MLP scores higher than the aux variant on BRCA and COADREAD and higher than the plain variant on BLCA and BRCA; the fusion models are ahead on STAD (+0.04 to +0.06), where RNA alone is weak, and on HNSC. No per-cohort difference reaches p < 0.05 before or after Holm correction. Separating "pathway tokens help" from "fusion helps" would need an MLP that receives the same pathway tokens, which has not been run.

### 4.3 Secondary metrics (`scripts/primary_tests.py` -> `results/final/table_secondary_metrics.txt`)

Uno's IPCW C-index (truncated at the 75th percentile of training event times) and the integrated Brier score (interior quartile grid; lower is better), 20-epoch DSS runs, mean +- sample sd over three seeds of the five-fold mean, with the seed-averaged paired difference vs SurvPath (95 % bootstrap CI, t p / W p). The IBS is undefined on BRCA fold 4 for every method (that fold is dropped from the BRCA cell and from the paired units, n = 24).

| IBS, BLCA / BRCA* / COADREAD / HNSC / STAD | 0.205 / 0.073 / 0.077 / 0.221 / 0.201 | 0.210 / 0.082 / 0.081 / 0.215 / 0.189 | 0.202 / 0.077 / 0.097 / 0.205 / 0.208 | 0.191 / 0.075 / 0.082 / 0.200 / 0.204 | 0.268 / 0.131 / 0.110 / 0.341 / 0.276 |

Uno's C tracks Harrell's C (same ordering, same significance pattern: the plain variant's margin is significant under both tests, the aux variant's under the Wilcoxon test only). Every other method beats SurvPath on the IBS by about 0.07: SurvPath's hazards are poorly calibrated under this protocol (its published loss weights the censored term by 0.5), so the IBS is not a fair accuracy comparison and is reported for completeness. Per-run IPCW C, IBS and td-AUC values are in `pod_results/outputs_e20/<run>/<cohort>/summary.md`; none was used for any decision.

### 4.4 Primary tests with confidence intervals and Holm correction (`scripts/primary_tests.py` -> `results/final/table_primary_tests.txt`)

Unit of analysis: one value per (cohort, fold) = mean over the seeds available for both methods, paired over the 25 pooled folds; 95 % percentile-bootstrap CI of the mean difference (10,000 resamples of folds, `numpy default_rng(0)`); paired t-test and two-sided exact Wilcoxon signed-rank test; per-cohort tests (n = 5) Holm-adjusted over the five cohorts (t and W separately; the pooled test is not part of that family). The script also verifies, while loading, that every trained fold's reported C-index equals its last-epoch validation C-index (no checkpoint selection).

| ABMIL vs SurvPath | DSS, seeds 0-2 | +0.001 | [-0.024, +0.026] | 0.95 | 0.85 | 14/25 |

Holm-adjusted per-cohort results: for PathQ-Former + aux vs SurvPath (DSS) the smallest adjusted p is BRCA (t 0.084, W 0.312); for PathQ-Former vs SurvPath, BRCA (t 0.367, W 0.625); for the OS comparison, BLCA (t 0.039, W 0.312) and BRCA (t 0.058, W 0.312). No DSS cohort survives correction for any comparison.

## 5. Input-use audit and missing-modality robustness (`scripts/missing_modality_table.py` -> `results/final/table_missing_modality_seeds.txt`)

### 5.1 The audit: the same 20-epoch checkpoint with one input removed or permuted (three seeds)

Each checkpoint is evaluated on its validation fold under five conditions: complete; RNA removed; RNA permuted across the validation patients (every patient gets a real but wrong profile); WSI removed; WSI permuted. A removed input is the learned null code for PathQ-Former and the training-mean gene vector or patch embedding for SurvPath (`scripts/eval_missing_impute.py --permute`; SurvPath cannot run without both inputs). Permutation is the stronger test: a mean or null input is neutral, a permuted input is plausible and wrong, so a model that reads it must lose concordance. Cells: mean +- sample sd over three seeds of the five-fold mean; delta: pooled difference from Complete over the 25 seed-averaged folds with t p / W p. The variant without aux heads was not evaluated under permutation (n/a).

| Condition | BLCA | BRCA | COADREAD | HNSC | STAD | delta (t p / W p) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SurvPath (official), mean imputation** | | | | | | |
| Complete | 0.594 +- 0.012 | 0.536 +- 0.026 | 0.570 +- 0.038 | 0.552 +- 0.019 | 0.587 +- 0.008 | |
| RNA removed | 0.595 +- 0.013 | 0.536 +- 0.027 | 0.572 +- 0.037 | 0.553 +- 0.018 | 0.588 +- 0.007 | +0.001 (0.12 / 0.085) |
| RNA permuted | 0.594 +- 0.013 | 0.537 +- 0.028 | 0.572 +- 0.038 | 0.552 +- 0.011 | 0.587 +- 0.006 | +0.001 (0.36 / 0.13) |
| WSI removed | 0.486 +- 0.022 | 0.520 +- 0.025 | 0.473 +- 0.012 | 0.504 +- 0.043 | 0.493 +- 0.082 | -0.073 (0.003 / 0.002) |
| WSI permuted | 0.511 +- 0.018 | 0.532 +- 0.052 | 0.510 +- 0.024 | 0.489 +- 0.033 | 0.459 +- 0.016 | -0.068 (0.016 / 0.007) |
| **PathQ-Former (no aux heads), null codes** | | | | | | |
| Complete | 0.609 +- 0.016 | 0.611 +- 0.039 | 0.638 +- 0.031 | 0.575 +- 0.012 | 0.593 +- 0.015 | |
| RNA removed | 0.612 +- 0.020 | 0.600 +- 0.046 | 0.633 +- 0.027 | 0.588 +- 0.008 | 0.595 +- 0.021 | +0.000 (0.96 / 0.51) |
| WSI removed | 0.590 +- 0.050 | 0.572 +- 0.033 | 0.601 +- 0.056 | 0.533 +- 0.017 | 0.578 +- 0.035 | -0.030 (0.080 / 0.16) |
| WSI removed, mean imputation instead (one seed) | 0.524 | 0.499 | 0.600 | 0.535 | 0.524 | -0.069 (3e-4 / 2.5e-4) |
| **PathQ-Former + aux heads, null codes** | | | | | | |
| Complete | 0.630 +- 0.010 | 0.622 +- 0.033 | 0.613 +- 0.023 | 0.582 +- 0.025 | 0.572 +- 0.022 | |
| RNA removed | 0.600 +- 0.002 | 0.592 +- 0.047 | 0.576 +- 0.025 | 0.596 +- 0.016 | 0.589 +- 0.010 | -0.013 (0.27 / 0.43) |
| RNA permuted | 0.597 +- 0.010 | 0.572 +- 0.046 | 0.618 +- 0.028 | 0.566 +- 0.019 | 0.555 +- 0.007 | -0.023 (0.075 / 0.063) |
| WSI removed | 0.613 +- 0.022 | 0.617 +- 0.052 | 0.583 +- 0.022 | 0.545 +- 0.026 | 0.538 +- 0.004 | -0.025 (0.19 / 0.11) |
| WSI permuted | 0.570 +- 0.035 | 0.539 +- 0.027 | 0.556 +- 0.033 | 0.539 +- 0.058 | 0.484 +- 0.035 | -0.067 (2e-4 / 4e-4) |
| RNA removed, mean imputation instead | 0.597 +- 0.003 | 0.607 +- 0.035 | 0.602 +- 0.012 | 0.589 +- 0.014 | 0.581 +- 0.018 | -0.009 (0.29 / 0.49) |
| WSI removed, mean imputation instead | 0.595 +- 0.027 | 0.591 +- 0.060 | 0.580 +- 0.016 | 0.558 +- 0.024 | 0.521 +- 0.037 | -0.035 (0.040 / 0.045) |

Findings:

- **SurvPath's ranking does not respond to its RNA input.** The model ranks patients the same way with their own profile, the training mean or another patient's profile (+0.001 in both cases); permuting the slide costs 0.068 and removing it 0.073, leaving 0.47-0.52 (removed) and 0.46-0.53 (permuted) on every cohort. The smallest change is on BRCA (-0.016), where its complete-input score (0.536) is already close to chance.
- **Null codes and modality dropout remove the collapse without the slide.** The variant without aux heads is as blind to RNA removal as SurvPath (+0.000) but loses only 0.030 without the slide; the same checkpoints lose 0.069, the size of SurvPath's collapse, when the removed slide is replaced by the training-mean patch embedding instead of the null code. With aux heads the null code loses 0.025 against 0.035 under mean imputation.
- **The auxiliary heads make the fused output respond to RNA.** With them the fused prediction loses 0.013 when RNA is removed and 0.023 when it is permuted (p 0.075 / 0.063 over 25 folds, short of 0.05; the attribution rests on the direction, on a wrong profile costing more than a null one, and on the contrast with the +0.000 / +0.001 of the other two models), against 0.067 when the slide is permuted. The checkpoint keeps 0.54-0.62 with either input removed. The RNA-permuted loss is a third of the slide-permuted loss: the fused prediction is histology-led but not histology-only (Section 5.3).
- Coverage, not accuracy: with RNA removed the single PathQ-Former checkpoint scores 0.576-0.600 against 0.553-0.587 for ABMIL (higher on four cohorts, lower on COADREAD); with the slide removed 0.538-0.617 against 0.532-0.633 for the RNA MLP (higher on BLCA and STAD, lower on BRCA, COADREAD and HNSC, by up to 0.050 on COADREAD).

### 5.2 Random partial missingness (three seeds; 10 / 20 / 30 / 50 % of validation patients missing one modality at random, 5 draws per fold)

| Cohort | PathQ+aux: full | 10 % | 20 % | 30 % | 50 % | PathQ (no aux): full | 10 % | 20 % | 30 % | 50 % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLCA | 0.630 | 0.630 | 0.625 | 0.627 | 0.621 | 0.609 | 0.606 | 0.609 | 0.608 | 0.603 |
| BRCA | 0.622 | 0.622 | 0.608 | 0.620 | 0.597 | 0.611 | 0.609 | 0.602 | 0.607 | 0.593 |
| COADREAD | 0.613 | 0.611 | 0.612 | 0.600 | 0.597 | 0.638 | 0.640 | 0.637 | 0.631 | 0.627 |
| HNSC | 0.582 | 0.577 | 0.577 | 0.581 | 0.572 | 0.575 | 0.571 | 0.571 | 0.569 | 0.562 |
| STAD | 0.572 | 0.571 | 0.571 | 0.574 | 0.557 | 0.593 | 0.590 | 0.584 | 0.594 | 0.576 |

With half of the validation patients missing one modality the fused C-index of PathQ-Former + aux changes by at most 0.025 (BRCA) and that of the variant without aux heads by at most 0.018 (BRCA); for the aux variant every change is within one seed standard deviation of the complete-input score. A site with mixed availability can instead route slide-only patients to ABMIL and RNA-only patients to the RNA MLP, or average two unimodal models; routing and late fusion are robust by construction and the late-fusion ensemble matches the joint model (Section 6). The one-checkpoint result is about coverage, not accuracy.

## 6. Is fusion doing anything? Joint fusion vs single-modality vs ensemble

### 6.1 All cohorts, 20 epochs (`results/final/table_fusion_vs_ensemble.txt`; joint models 3 seeds, late fusion seeds 0-1, single-modality PathQ-Formers 3 seeds except BRCA with 2)

| Cohort | PathQ+aux (joint) | PathQ (joint, no aux) | Late fusion (WSI-only + RNA-only PathQ, same seed) | WSI-only PathQ | RNA-only PathQ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLCA | 0.630 +- 0.010 | 0.609 +- 0.016 | 0.629 +- 0.018 | 0.592 +- 0.003 | 0.608 +- 0.020 |
| BRCA | 0.622 +- 0.033 | 0.611 +- 0.039 | 0.606 +- 0.020 | 0.615 +- 0.027 | 0.559 +- 0.001 |
| COADREAD | 0.613 +- 0.023 | 0.638 +- 0.031 | 0.620 +- 0.069 | 0.574 +- 0.024 | 0.598 +- 0.035 |
| HNSC | 0.582 +- 0.025 | 0.575 +- 0.012 | 0.571 +- 0.009 | 0.585 +- 0.003 | 0.554 +- 0.013 |
| STAD | 0.572 +- 0.022 | 0.593 +- 0.015 | 0.544 +- 0.006 | 0.582 +- 0.019 | 0.511 +- 0.005 |

With both sides restricted to seeds 0-1 (Section 4.4), the joint PathQ-Former + aux is +0.011 over the late-fusion ensemble (95 % CI [-0.013, +0.034]; t p 0.39, W p 0.28; 14/25 folds) and the variant without aux heads +0.009 ([-0.020, +0.036]; p 0.54 / 0.52). Joint fusion is therefore worth about an ensemble of the two branches; the fusion block does not extract complementarity beyond that, and the manuscript says so.

### 6.2 BLCA fusion ablations (10-epoch budget, seed 0)

| Variant | C-index |
|---|---|
| base | 0.609 |
| modality dropout 0 / 0.3 / 0.5 | 0.634 / 0.616 / 0.635 |
| K = 16 / 64 queries | 0.638 / 0.634 |
| fusion depth 1 / 3 | 0.598 / 0.595 |
| joint (3 seeds) / late fusion / WSI-only / RNA-only | 0.618 / 0.631 / 0.596 / 0.603 |

None of K, fusion depth or modality dropout moves the fused score outside one fold-std (0.60-0.64). Modality dropout matters only for missing-modality robustness (0.3 was best there). The test-time single-modality scores of the same checkpoints were as high as the fused score (md30: fused 0.616, WSI-only 0.624, RNA-only 0.648), which was the observation that motivated the auxiliary heads.

| Cohort | PathQ+aux | SurvPath | delta | paired t p (5 folds) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLCA | **0.595** | 0.552 | +0.043 | 0.008 |
| BRCA | **0.596** | 0.523 | +0.073 | 0.015 |
| COADREAD | 0.581 | **0.596** | -0.015 | 0.58 |

Holm-adjusted over the five cohorts: BLCA t 0.039 (Wilcoxon 0.312), BRCA t 0.058 (0.312), HNSC t 0.138 (0.375); BLCA, the development cohort, is the only cohort that survives correction, under the t-test only. ## 8. Ablations of the final configuration (BLCA, PathQ+aux, 20 ep, seed 0, laptop CPU; `pod_results/laptop_runs.tgz` -> `results/final/table_final_config_ablations.txt`)

Five-fold mean C-index of the same checkpoint with both inputs, with the slide removed (RNA-only, null code), with the RNA removed (WSI-only), and with 50 % of validation patients randomly missing one modality; one seed, so no spread over seeds is given.

| Variant | Both | WSI-only | RNA-only | 50 % missing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default: 4 bins, Reactome+Hallmark 275 pathways, all patches (seed 0 / 3-seed mean) | 0.625 / 0.630 | 0.598 / 0.600 | 0.588 / 0.613 | - / 0.621 |
| 2 hazard bins (`pathq_aux_e20_bins2`) | 0.628 | 0.634 | 0.575 | 0.616 |
| 8 hazard bins (`pathq_aux_e20_bins8`) | 0.609 | 0.578 | 0.605 | 0.604 |
| Xena 281 pathways (`pathq_aux_e20_xena`) | 0.628 | 0.604 | 0.634 | 0.615 |
| Hallmark-only 50 pathways (`pathq_aux_e20_hallmarks`) | 0.600 | 0.608 | 0.554 | 0.597 |
| 4096 training patches instead of all (`pathq_aux_e20_patches4096`) | 0.626 | 0.591 | 0.622 | 0.611 |

The 2-bin run was also evaluated under permutation: RNA permuted 0.619 (-0.009), WSI permuted 0.571 (-0.057).

- Bin count: 2 ~ 4 > 8, all within one fold-std; 8 bins spreads too few events per bin. (With 2 bins the Brier grid has no interior edge, so IBS is undefined; C-index is unaffected.)
- Pathway set: the two 275-281-pathway sets are equivalent; Hallmark-only costs ~0.03. The genomic branch benefits from many small pathway tokens.
- Patch budget: training on a 4096-patch subsample gives the same score as all patches. PathQ-Former's edge over SurvPath (which trains on 4096) is therefore not explained by patch count.

## 9. Efficiency (`scripts/efficiency.py`; RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell; BLCA fold-0 validation, 40 real patients, medians)

| Model | Params (M) | Patches | Forward (ms) | Forward + backward (ms) | Peak GPU memory (GiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PathQ-Former (all patches) | 16.9 | 6214 | 35.0 | 104.2 | 1.17 |
| PathQ-Former (4096 patches) | 16.9 | 4096 | 34.7 | 104.1 | 0.17 |
| SurvPath (4096 patches, as trained) | 21.2 | 4096 | 35.7 | 175.6 | 0.20 |
| SurvPath (all patches) | 21.2 | 6214 | 36.0 | 176.0 | 1.74 |

PathQ-Former's compute is dominated by the 32-query cross-attention, so latency is flat in the number of patches; SurvPath's patch-pathway co-attention grows with both. On the laptop CPU with a 36k-patch slide: PathQ-Former 190 ms forward / 1013 ms step, SurvPath 188 / 724 ms (both ~45 / ~215 ms at 4096 patches). Training throughput on the pods was I/O-bound (feature reads from the network volume), not model-bound.

## 10. Validity: what the numbers do and do not support

**Supported**

- The official SurvPath implementation, under an equal-budget protocol on five TCGA cohorts, ranks patients the same way with its RNA input present, replaced by the training mean or permuted across patients (+0.001), and collapses without the slide (0.47-0.52). Removal and permutation audits with risk-score correlations detect this without any training (Section 5).
- Null codes and modality dropout remove the collapse without the slide (-0.030 with the null code, -0.069 under mean imputation on the same checkpoints, -0.073 for SurvPath); auxiliary unimodal heads make the fused output respond to RNA (-0.023 under permutation); one checkpoint keeps 0.54-0.62 with either input removed and moves by at most 0.025 at 50 % missingness.
- Accuracy at equal budget: parity with an RNA-only MLP and a late-fusion ensemble; +0.036 / +0.037 over the untuned SurvPath pooled, significant under the Wilcoxon test for both variants and under the t-test for the variant without aux heads only; no DSS cohort survives Holm correction. Reproduced on OS with one seed (+0.034, [+0.014, +0.054]).
- Validation-loss early stopping, replayed on the stored histories, selects epoch 1-3 checkpoints on these event-poor folds and costs the late-learning models up to 0.09 C-index and SurvPath nothing (Section 3.3).

**Not supported / must be stated**

- No accuracy superiority over SurvPath is claimed: SurvPath was not re-tuned, PathQ-Former's hyper-parameters were developed on BLCA, and the aux-head variant was adopted after the 20-epoch results had been seen, so the comparison is favourable to PathQ-Former by an amount that cannot be bounded without tuning the baseline.
- PathQ-Former is not detectably better than the RNA-only MLP pooled (+0.012 / +0.014; CIs include 0) and the MLP scores higher on two of five cohorts; fusion is worth about an ensemble of the two branches (+0.011 / +0.009 over late fusion, n.s.). Do not claim complementarity beyond an ensemble.
- The RNA-permuted loss of 0.023 that supports the auxiliary-head claim has p 0.075 / 0.063 over 25 folds.
- The recipe has not been applied to SurvPath (implemented, not run; Section 14), so how much of the robustness is specific to the query bottleneck is untested.
- Per-cohort tests have five folds; the fold-level sd of the C-index is 0.14-0.25 on COADREAD for the fusion models (0.12-0.16 for SurvPath); BLCA, the development cohort, is the only cohort that survives Holm on OS (t-test only).
- Comparison to published numbers is indirect: our protocol (DSS, patient-level, fixed budget, final checkpoint) differs from each paper's; the meaningful reference is the official SurvPath code under our protocol.
- Missingness is simulated at random and therefore uninformative; TCGA only, frozen UNI2-h features whose pretraining corpus may include TCGA slides; no clinical covariates; no external cohort.
- Single seed for the OS endpoint and for the mean-imputation evaluation of the variant without aux heads; two seeds for late fusion; three seeds for everything else except the BRCA cells of the single-modality PathQ-Formers (two).

**History of the statistics.** The seed-averaged tests were introduced on 2026-09-22 (EXPERIMENT_LOG.md, section "Reviewer-requested recomputes") and the permutation test and three-seed imputation on 2026-09-23 ("Batch 9 part 1"); the bootstrap CIs, the Holm correction, the secondary-metric tests and the selection replay were added in the 2026-10-05 revision. Until that revision this report quoted the 75-pair (fold, seed) tests (t p 0.002 / 0.007) as the headline; they are superseded by Section 4.4.

**Known sources of variance**: 5-45 events per validation fold; fold 3 of BLCA is weak for every method; fold 0 of COADREAD (5 events) scores 0.84-0.92 for the two PathQ-Former variants and 0.66-0.89 for SurvPath over the three seeds.

## 11. Engineering record

**Pipeline** (`src/`): `data/tcga_dataset.py` (patient-level dataset, training-fit bins and scaler, optional fp16 RAM cache capped at a fraction of the container's cgroup memory limit), `models/pathqformer.py`, `models/baselines.py` (ABMIL, SNN, MLP, official SurvPath wrapper), `training/evaluate.py` (all metrics, bootstrap, KM), `training/train.py` (5-fold CV with two-level resume: finished folds and mid-fold checkpoints; `--set key=value` overrides; RAdam; weighted sampling; auxiliary loss masked to present samples).

**Analysis scripts** (`scripts/`): `reproduce_tables.sh` (extracts the five archives and regenerates `results/final/`), `seed_table.py` (seeded tables with paired tests over pairs and over seed-averaged folds), `primary_tests.py` (seed-averaged tests with bootstrap CIs and Holm correction; secondary metrics), `missing_modality_table.py` (audit conditions over seeds), `risk_correlation.py`, `posthoc_selection.py` (selection-rule replay on the stored histories), `aggregate_results.py`, `epoch_curves.py`, `late_fusion.py`, `eval_missing_impute.py --permute` (mean imputation and permutation evaluations of a finished run), `efficiency.py`, `recompute_metrics.py` (re-derives all metric blocks from saved per-patient predictions so protocol changes apply retroactively), `analyze_run.py --attention` (attention export for figures), `paper_figures.py` and `paper_figures_km.py` (the manuscript's vector figures from the archives), `make_anonymous_supplement.py` (double-blind supplement with a self-check scan).

**Tests**: 46 tests (`pytest`; 35 fast incl. 8 for the SurvPath-recipe model, skipped without `data/survpath_repo`), 11 of them slow end-to-end trainer tests on dummy embeddings: overrides and validation, weighted sampler, OS/PFI endpoints, patients without embeddings, full CV run + fold skip, mid-fold resume, all three selection modes, seed determinism, auxiliary loss, every baseline through the trainer, every analysis script. Bugs the suite caught: `--set lr=1e-4` parsed as a string (YAML 1.1); bootstrap crash on resamples with no comparable pairs (COADREAD).

**Compute infrastructure**: Runpod pods (RTX PRO 4000/4500 Blackwell, RTX 2000 Ada) sharing a 250 GB network volume (fjb5dlrrfp, EU-RO-1) with all five cohorts' UNI2-h features, outputs and logs; resumable queue scripts (`scripts/pod/`) that skip finished runs, chain batches, and remove their own pod; up to three pods in parallel. The checkpoints of the 180 runs archived by the 2026-09-19 pull (855 files, ~44 GB) remain on the volume.

**Incidents worth remembering**: (1) container OOM: `free` shows the host's 125 GB but the cgroup limit was 29-62 GB; the cache is now sized from `memory.max`. (2) Early-stopping-by-val-loss protocol failure on event-poor cohorts (Section 3.2). (3) Pod self-removal failed twice on `runpodctl` version differences; the v1/v2/REST three-way chain in `run_queue_pod.sh` is the fix, and a hand-written watcher that skipped it cost ~13 idle hours (~8 USD). (4) The account balance reached zero once and Runpod deleted every pod, including one unrelated to this project; the volume kept everything and the interrupted run resumed from its saved folds.

## 13. Recommended paper framing

**Title-level claim** (as revised in `paper/tmlr_v2/main.tex`): do histology-transcriptomics survival models use both inputs? A missing-modality audit shows that the official SurvPath implementation's ranking does not respond to its RNA input and collapses without the slide; a one-checkpoint training recipe (null codes, modality dropout, auxiliary unimodal heads) removes the collapse and makes the fused output respond to RNA, at parity with the best unimodal baseline and a late-fusion ensemble. No accuracy superiority over SurvPath is claimed.

**Contributions**: (1) the input-use audit (removal, permutation across patients, risk-score correlation; 3 seeds x 5 folds x 5 cohorts) applied to a published co-attention model under an equal-budget protocol (Section 5); (2) evidence on where missing-modality robustness comes from, from matched variants of one fusion model (Sections 5-6); (3) protocol evidence: seed-aware statistics with bootstrap CIs and Holm correction (Section 4.4) and the post-hoc replay of checkpoint selection on event-poor folds (Section 3.3).

**Tables**: audit = Section 5.1; accuracy = Sections 4.1 and 4.4; missing-rate sweep = Section 5.2 as a figure; selection replay = Section 3.3; appendix: per-cohort Holm tests, OS, 10-epoch budget, secondary metrics (4.3), risk correlations (5.3), null code vs mean imputation, fusion ablations (6.2), efficiency (9).
**Figures** (`scripts/paper_figures.py`, `scripts/paper_figures_km.py`): audit deltas with bootstrap CIs, missing-rate curves over seeds, pooled epoch curves, KM grid, pathway attention.

**Limitations to state**: baseline not re-tuned and variant selected after the results were seen; recipe not applied to SurvPath; three seeds, five folds per cohort, the RNA-permuted loss at p 0.075 / 0.063; TCGA only, frozen UNI2-h features, random missingness, no clinical covariates, no external cohort.

3. **Pending from batch 9**: BRCA seed-2 single-modality pair and late fusion seed 2; the 34-cell SurvPath learning-rate x alpha grid (1 of 35 cells run).
4. **Optional**: a pathway-token input for the MLP baseline (to separate "pathway tokens help" from "fusion helps"); an external cohort for the robustness claim.
5. **Housekeeping**: the network volume still holds the checkpoints and the batch-10 partial output; rotate the HuggingFace and Runpod credentials used during the campaign.

## Appendix A. Reproducing the tables

`bash scripts/reproduce_tables.sh` extracts the five archives (`pod_results/pod_results.tgz`, `pull_0918/results_0918a.tgz`, `pull_0918/results_0918b.tgz`, `pull_0923/results_0923.tgz`, `laptop_runs.tgz`) and writes every table of this report to `results/final/`; the individual commands it runs are:

```bash
# Sections 4.1, 4.2, 7, 3.2 (10 epochs), 6.1: seeded tables with paired tests over pairs and over seed-averaged folds
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/seed_table.py pod_results/outputs_e20 \
  --methods pathq_fast_e20 pathq_fast_e20_aux survpath_e20 abmil_e20 snn_e20 mlp_omics_e20 --ref survpath_e20
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/seed_table.py pod_results/outputs_e20 \
  --methods pathq_fast_e20 pathq_fast_e20_aux survpath_e20 mlp_omics_e20 --ref mlp_omics_e20
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/seed_table.py pod_results/outputs_os --methods pathq_fast_e20_aux survpath_e20 --ref survpath_e20
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/seed_table.py pod_results/outputs_v2 pod_results/outputs_ablate --methods pathq_fast_e10 survpath_e10 --ref survpath_e10
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/seed_table.py pod_results/outputs_e20 \
  --methods pathq_fast_e20_aux pathq_fast_e20 late_fusion_e20 pathq_e20_wsi_only pathq_e20_genomic_only --ref late_fusion_e20
# Section 5: audit conditions over seeds (removed, imputed, permuted, random missingness) and risk correlations
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/missing_modality_table.py pod_results/outputs_e20 --methods pathq_fast_e20_aux pathq_fast_e20 survpath_e20
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/risk_correlation.py pod_results/outputs_e20 --run pathq_fast_e20_aux --others survpath_e20 mlp_omics_e20 abmil_e20 snn_e20 pathq_fast_e20
# Section 3.3: selection-rule replay on the stored histories
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/posthoc_selection.py --roots pod_results/outputs_e20 pod_results/outputs_v2 pod_results/outputs_ablate \
  --v2-root pod_results/outputs_v2 --patience 5 --min-epochs 0 --out -
# Sections 4.3-4.4: primary tests with bootstrap CIs and Holm correction; secondary metrics
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/primary_tests.py --e20 pod_results/outputs_e20 --os pod_results/outputs_os --out-dir results/final
# Section 8: final-configuration ablations (laptop runs)
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/missing_modality_table.py pod_results/outputs_v2 \
  --methods pathq_aux_e20_bins2 pathq_aux_e20_bins8 pathq_aux_e20_hallmarks pathq_aux_e20_patches4096 pathq_aux_e20_xena
# per-run summaries; efficiency (measured on a pod, copied)
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/aggregate_results.py pod_results/outputs_e20 --out results/final/summary_e20_all_runs.md
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/aggregate_results.py pod_results/outputs_os --out results/final/summary_os_all_runs.md
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/aggregate_results.py pod_results/outputs_ablate --out results/final/summary_ablate_all_runs.md
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/aggregate_results.py pod_results/outputs_v2 --out results/final/summary_v2_all_runs.md
cp pod_results/outputs_e20/efficiency.md results/final/efficiency.md
```

To produce new evaluations rather than tables: `scripts/eval_missing_impute.py <run_dir> --permute` (imputation and permutation conditions for a finished run), `scripts/late_fusion.py <run_a> <run_b> --out ...`, `scripts/epoch_curves.py <roots>`. Per-run artefacts: `pod_results/outputs_*/<run>/<cohort>/{results.json, summary.md, config.yaml, fold_k/}`. Final configurations: `configs/protocol_fixed/`; ablations: `configs/ablation_fixed/`.
